### New

- **Hide Lightning Flashes.** Turning on **Hide Lightning Flashes** in Minecraft's Accessibility settings now also turns off the lyrics' flashes: the glow pulse, the crosshair flash, the hat flare, the sky pulse and the World words' white flash when they appear.
- **Distortion Effects.** Minecraft's **Distortion Effects** setting (in Accessibility settings) now also calms the lyrics' motion: at 0 the line pop, the World words' sway, knock and arrival bounce, and the hat's wobble and spin (without a jump when you move the slider) and the spinning record in the top bar and on the **Record card** stay still, and in between they are slower or smaller.
- **Demo song.** While the demo song plays, the top bar shows "Demo" next to the song, so you can tell it from your own music. Switching the demo song on now starts it from the top, playing, instead of somewhere in the middle (or still paused from last time). Turning **Demo song** off while the song library is open brings your own songs back instead of keeping the made-up ones.
- **Can't read your music player.** If SkyLyrics can't read your music player (or can't reach the internet for Spotify) for 10 seconds, it now tells you with a pop-up, once per game start, and where to look.
- **Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese.** The settings, song library, top bar, Record card and tour are now in Spanish (Spain and Latin America) and Brazilian Portuguese (also used for Portugal), with Minecraft's own names for its menus.
- **Smooth letters for more alphabets.** Russian, Ukrainian and other Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese lyrics use smooth letters like the rest of the line instead of small pixel ones.

### Fixed

- **Player list and action bar.** Holding Tab on a server no longer draws the player list over the top bar or a **Record card** in a top corner: they fade out while it shows and back when you let go. A bottom bar no longer lifts when a server sends an empty action bar message to clear it.
- **Sky effects fade.** The sky effects now fade in and out smoothly when the time of day jumps (/time set, or a server skipping the night) instead of cutting in a single frame. Changing **Night sky** while it is night fades the old sky out before the new one comes in. With **Pulse with the lyrics** on and no synced lyrics showing (unsynced lyrics, no lyrics, an instrumental song, or lyrics hidden), the sky is no longer a little dimmer than with it off. The sparkles no longer drift in from a stale spot when they come back. On 1.21.11 and newer, in light rain the sky effects are no longer dimmer than they should be. They also fade out while a boss bar pulls the fog in (some servers' boss bars do), like the vanilla sky.
- **Pick a look crash.** Pressing Left or Right on **Pick a look** while the look is Custom (after changing any look setting) no longer crashes the game: Right picks the first look and Left the last.
- **Intro look.** The first-run tour's look page now starts on your current look (or says Custom) instead of Neon, and the next and previous buttons step from it.
- **Updates on Windows.** Automatic updates now install for players whose Windows user name has letters beyond plain English ones (Hebrew, Cyrillic, accented) or spaces and signs. An update can no longer leave you without SkyLyrics: the old file is only deleted once the new one is in place, and it is put back if the new one can't be. A download that Windows briefly holds is tried again, and old update leftovers are cleaned up.
- **Saving on Windows.** Settings, the recently heard list, the Spotify sign-in and saved covers are read and saved even when Windows, an antivirus or OneDrive holds the file for a moment (the mod tries again), and the Windows music reader's helper file is written the same careful way.
- **Right lyrics for the right song.** A song title like "Levels - Skrillex Remix" in a browser is no longer split into a made-up artist and song, and "Song | Official Music Video" is looked up as "Song" (a timing you saved for one of these browser songs has to be set again). The NetEase backup now finds a song whose title has a tag like "(Remastered 2011)". With no song length (browsers, some local files), an exact title wins over "Song (Live)". Full-width letters match plain ones. With the Spotify app on Linux, two songs with the same name, artist and album are told apart. A title with a version tag in brackets, like "Song (2011 Remaster)", is also looked up without it when nothing is found.
- **Updates that wouldn't start.** An update that needs a newer Minecraft or Fabric API than you have is no longer installed: the mod tells you what to update instead, and your working version stays. It remembers this, so the same update is not downloaded again on every start until you update Fabric API, Fabric Loader, Minecraft or Java, or a newer release comes out.
- **Fabric API too old.** With a Fabric API that is too old for SkyLyrics, Minecraft now tells you which version to install instead of crashing at start. The 1.21.10 download no longer says it works on 1.21.9, because no Fabric API for 1.21.9 has what it needs.
- **Mixed-direction lines.** In the Arc layout, and in World with **Flowing line** on, a Hebrew or Arabic line with an English phrase in it (or an English line with a Hebrew phrase) now reads each part in its own direction, so "NYC 2024" no longer comes out as "2024 NYC". Quotes and signs like « » ‹ › ≤ ≥ now turn the right way in Hebrew and Arabic text, and Arabic words in the Arc layout are spaced to fit.
- **Two games at once.** Two Minecraft games open at the same time (sharing one game folder) no longer undo each other's settings or song timings: when one saves, it keeps what the other changed, and shows it too. The song library's **Recently heard** list keeps the songs both games heard. Saving at the same moment no longer breaks the settings file or loses a renewed Spotify sign-in, and when two games renew the Spotify sign-in together, the second one waits a moment for the first one's new sign-in instead of signing you out. On Windows, a second game no longer deletes the first one's album covers. When both games update, neither deletes the new mod file the other just installed (on Windows too), and a backup of yours in the mods folder ending in .old is never touched.
- **Long titles.** A very long song title, especially one with a bracket left open, no longer makes the lyrics lookup hang.
- **Long words in the top bar.** A word wider than the top bar (a web address, a long compound word, a line of one long word) now shows its start while it is sung instead of jumping to its end.
- **Crash leftovers.** If the game is closed by force while saving, the temporary files it leaves for the recently heard list, the update memory and the Windows music reader are now removed at the next start, including recently heard ones left by 0.8.0 and earlier.
- **Fast lines.** In World, the last words of a very short line (rap, fast lyrics) now show before the next line takes over, and the words of a short line start as it comes in. In Arc, words not yet shown fade in as a fast line leaves instead of all flashing on at once. In World, a very long word in a **Flowing line** no longer leaves a big gap before it.
- **Quick skips.** After a quick skip, the new song no longer shows the old song's lyrics, album cover or colour. The top bar, the **Record card** and the shooting stars no longer show the last song's line or "finding lyrics" next to the new song's name. A slow lyrics or album cover lookup for the old song no longer holds up the new one. A lookup cut short by a skip also no longer makes the mod use the backup lyrics site (NetEase) for two minutes, and no longer leaves a half-written lyrics file behind. A song also keeps its lyrics and album cover when one step of the song change fails.
- **Odd lyric files.** Lyrics with an hour in their time stamps, extra digits after the seconds, wide (full-width) brackets, spaces inside the brackets ("[ 00:12.00 ]"), an invisible space at the start of a line or odd hidden characters no longer lose lines or show as boxes.
- **NetEase lyrics.** When the lyrics come from the NetEase backup, a song whose words contain "纯音乐" (Chinese for "instrumental") no longer loses them; only NetEase's own "instrumental" placeholder counts.
- **Effects after loading.** With **Effects** on Auto, reloading resources or switching shaders no longer leaves the lyrics on Light effects for up to two minutes, and a single stutter no longer counts as a slow game (stutter that keeps coming still does).
- **Mac music player.** On a Mac, lyrics no longer run a little late, and a song with something missing (for example a local file or podcast with no album cover) still shows its title and lyrics.
- **Mac Spotify ads and radio.** On a Mac, a Spotify ad is no longer looked up as a song, and two songs with the same title, artist and album are told apart. Music's internet radio now shows the playing song instead of the station name.
- **Hidden direction marks.** Hebrew and Arabic titles that carry invisible left-to-right or right-to-left marks no longer draw boxes or miss their lyrics, and lyric lines that carry such marks no longer draw them as boxes in the sky, the top bar or the **Record card**: the marks still set the word order.
- **Hebrew settings text.** With the game in Hebrew, lines in the settings, the intro tour and the song library that start with an English word ("Beli's SkyLyrics…", "NetEase Cloud Music…") now read right to left like the rest of their paragraph, and so does the settings footer ("J או Esc לסגירה").
- **Settings search.** In a Hebrew game, an English word now finds every setting it names, also where two English words share one Hebrew word (Position and Placement, Words and Lyrics, Arc and Rainbow). Search ignores accents, Hebrew vowel marks and final letter forms, and the invisible marks and odd spaces that pasted text can carry. With the Narrator on, it says how many settings were found. Long result headings are cut to fit the window.
- **Hebrew and Arabic numbers.** With the game in Hebrew or Arabic, the **Record card**'s time left reads "-2:35" instead of "2:35-", and the **Height**, **Distance** and **Size** sliders read the right way round ("-10°", "0.50×"). In every language, the time left at the end of a song reads "0:00", not "-0:00".
- **Windows album cover.** A cover that the player corrects a few seconds into a song (the first one was the last song's, for example on YouTube in Edge or Chrome) now replaces the wrong one on screen. A Windows PC that blocks the music reader no longer has it retried every 15 seconds all session: the waits grow up to 5 minutes and the warning is logged once. The recently heard list no longer remembers a Windows cover's temporary file.
- **Windows music player.** A player that resumes no longer makes the lyrics skip ahead and back, and one that never says when it updated no longer freezes the lyrics. An album cover that stalls no longer makes the link to your music player time out and restart, and a player that is slow to answer once no longer makes the lyrics blink away. An album cover that was still the last song's is read again a few seconds later. Pause, Skip and Seek no longer reach another app when the one you follow has closed.
- **World words stay put.** On Linux, a music player that answers slowly, or Spotify right after a pause or resume, no longer makes the World words vanish for a moment. Moving the **Timing** slider no longer makes them blink.
- **World title.** In the World layout the song title shows for its full time even when the lyrics take a moment to load, and a long title is shrunk to fit.
- **World after respawning.** Respawning or changing world during the end of a line no longer flashes its last words, and a word more than 48 blocks away fades out instead of vanishing. Swinging your arm while the World lyrics are hidden no longer knocks a word when they show again.
- **Song library.** Songs in a long list show up right away as you scroll, and can't be clicked before they appear. If more of a list fails to load, the library tries again a few times by itself; in the grid view you can also click the error line. Spotify playlists with local files or podcasts no longer repeat songs or stop loading partway. Scrolling the recently heard list can no longer cause an error. Pressing Space on a playlist opens it without jumping to search. Pressing Enter after changing the search no longer plays a song from the old results. Play no longer waits behind searches (a busy Spotify could leave it doing nothing for up to 30 seconds), searches you typed past are dropped, old results can't be picked while you are still typing, a double-click on a playlist no longer plays a song from it, the local Spotify app is tried even when Spotify can't list your devices, and a long "Nothing found" text is cut to fit.
- **Open song library key.** With Iris installed, an **Open song library** key you set to K (the same key as Iris's shader switch) is moved back to N only once, not on every start.
- **Album covers.** An album cover shows even when it can't be saved for next time, and a damaged saved album cover is fetched again. One that couldn't download (no network, a slow or busy server) is tried again every so often during the song, instead of staying missing until the next song. One that stalls while downloading is cut off instead of blocking the next song's album cover. An album cover the game can't read, or a song with the same name as an earlier one but another album cover, no longer keeps the earlier song's colour.
- **Bottom bar and Record card.** The bottom bar sits above the held item's name, above the hearts and armour when you have several rows of them, and above the text that a jukebox or a command shows over the hotbar. A bigger **Bar size** grows upward instead of off the screen. On a narrow screen a big **Bar size** now fits: the bar shrinks and, if needed, hides the stats and then the clock. The **Record card** in a bottom corner now sits above the bar instead of covering it, and above the armour and the held item's name.
- **Top bar and Record card.** The top bar, and the **Record card** in a top corner, hide while the debug screen (F3) is showing. They also fade to black with the rest of the screen when you sleep, instead of staying bright over it. A top bar on a medium-wide screen moves down below the potion effect icons when its numbers would reach them, and the **Record card** in a top corner moves below the boss bars on a narrow screen. A **Record card** in a top corner with the top bar at the top no longer sits on top of the bar on a small window or a big GUI scale: it moves down below it. A song title that fits no longer ends with a lone "…" where the artist would be.
- **Minecraft 1.21.1 to 1.21.5.** On 1.21.1 the top bar's text is clipped right at every **Bar size**, and the lyrics, bar and card no longer cover the chat. On 1.21.1 to 1.21.5, setting descriptions are no longer cut off at the edge of the list.
- **Caves and the Nether.** **Show underground too** now also works in the Nether (when **See through blocks** is off). Swimming deep underwater no longer counts as being in a cave.
- **Spyglass and sky lines.** The thin lines of the painted skies (Synthwave, Moonlight) and the constellations keep their width while you zoom with a spyglass, and with Speed or sprinting, instead of getting about 11 times too thick when zoomed.
- **Sky effects.** With **Lazy follow** on or off, the sparkles and shooting stars now follow your view the same way the lyrics do, and they change line at the same moment as the words. They stay visible in front of the eclipse. With the World layout, the sparkles stay with the words even when **Lazy follow** was left on from another layout.
- **Sky fades.** The sky fades back in after leaving the Nether or the End, or coming up out of water, instead of popping in. It fades out under Blindness and Darkness, as the vanilla sky does. The Comet sky no longer flickers on 26.2 and later.
- **Propeller.** With **Glow with the lyrics** off, the propeller cap turns at its calm speed.
- **Lyrics stuck in the wrong place.** In a rare case where the game gave a broken camera position, the lyrics could stay pinned in the wrong place or the **View lock** could stick. They now recover.
- **Clicks on 26.3.** On Minecraft 26.3, a click outside the game window no longer counts as a click inside it.
- **Linux music players.** When a launcher hides your session from the game, the mod now still finds your music players instead of saying it can't reach them. In a Flatpak (for example the Prism Launcher), when it isn't allowed to talk to music players and none show up, the mod now shows the Flatpak hint instead of just "nothing playing".
- **Players with long names.** On Linux, players such as Amberol are now shown by their own name, and songs from the library open in the right player.
- **Players without a position.** A player that doesn't say where it is in the song no longer holds the lyrics on the first line; they keep time from when the song started or resumed.
- **Spotify gaps.** With Spotify, a moment when Spotify says nothing is playing (around an ad, a track change or a switch to another device) no longer makes the lyrics blink out and come back up to 4 seconds late: the mod asks again after a second. With Spotify signed in, an ad is no longer taken for a song. A Spotify answer without a play state no longer causes an error.
- **Same name, two songs.** When one Spotify song follows another with the same title and artist (like two "Interlude"s), the mod now sees a new song: it looks up the second one's lyrics and starts them from the top instead of carrying on with the first one's. The two still share their per-song **Timing**.
- **Spotify messages.** A Spotify app that doesn't know your account now tells you to add it under User Management on the Spotify dashboard, instead of "error 403". If Spotify refuses your sign-in even after the mod renewed it, the mod says "Spotify signed you out, sign in again" instead of "error 401". When Spotify can't be reached, the settings show one steady message saying the internet can't be reached (it used to blink on and off and blame the player), and the log gets one warning instead of one a minute.
- **No crash from a drawing error.** A rare error in the mod's drawing no longer crashes the game: the part that failed pauses for 5 seconds and the error goes to the log.
- **Font mods.** Fixes a clash with other font mods on Minecraft 1.21.1 and 1.21.4, and a small memory leak when a letter can't be loaded.
- **Intro tour.** The intro tour fits small windows and big GUI scales. It no longer opens over a screen that replaced the title screen, and its last page says the keys work in a world.
- **Lyrics on the title screen.** In a tall, narrow window they're sized to fit the width instead of running off both sides. A button another mod puts in a bottom corner no longer pushes them down until they vanish; they stay under the menu buttons and keep clear of it.
- **Hand-edited settings file.** A blank or very long recent search in the settings file no longer breaks the song library, and a hand-typed player name like "Spotify-Web" now picks that player.
- **Locked or damaged settings.** If SkyLyrics still can't read your settings or recently heard file at start, it leaves the file alone and keeps a damaged copy next to it, instead of saving defaults over your settings. A settings or Spotify sign-in file left half-written when the game was killed is cleaned up the next time the game starts, once it is a day old.
- **Settings that did nothing.** In the World layout, the settings it doesn't use (**Draw on top**, **Depth**, **Shadow**, **Pulse**, **Karaoke fill** and **Bigger current word**) are hidden, as **Animation** already was. With Floating placement, **Distance** shows the real distance in blocks (for example "10.7 blocks" rather than "64 blocks"). **Strength** now shows when only **Constellations** is on, since it changes how bright they are, and **Sky speed** and **Pulse with the lyrics** show with **Constellations** and the other sky effects too. **Background** (how dark the bar is) also shows when only the Record card is on, since the card uses it.
- **Settings scroll.** **Open Music tab** in the song library now takes you down to the Spotify card every time. Settings tabs also keep their place after you visit a shorter tab.
- **Settings text.** A sky **Strength** of 0 in the settings file now shows as 10%, where the slider starts. Settings search also finds English words in a Hebrew game, and pasted search text is cleaned up like typed text. A few English and Hebrew texts say what they mean (the previous line, **Preview**, **Aurora**).
- **Height and Arc.** The **Height** setting is hidden for Arc when it has no effect (Floating, or Direction Follow), but still found by search. Changing Direction, Placement, Height or the view lock moves the Arc lines that use them right away instead of from the next line.
- **Faint glow on 1.21.1 to 1.21.5.** A very faint glow (the previous and next lines, the end of the pulse) no longer flashes as solid colour.
- **Instrumental and karaoke tracks.** "Song (Instrumental)", a karaoke, a backing track or an a cappella version no longer gets the lyrics of the sung song, and the other way round.
- **Elytra mode.** After a steep dive or climb, the words come back to where they were once you level out, instead of staying higher or lower.
- **Album covers with odd file names.** On Linux, a player that gives its album cover as a file with spaces or accents in the name, or in another odd file-address form, now shows it. On Windows, an album cover that the player gives as a web-style file address (starting with file://) shows too.
- **Stopped players.** On Linux, a player that is stopped (not just paused) but still remembers its last song (Rhythmbox, VLC) no longer keeps that song in the bar.
- **Music player blips.** On Linux, when your music player shows nothing for a second or two between songs, SkyLyrics no longer jumps to a browser tab and keeps showing its song.
- **No odd formatting from song text.** A song title, artist, album or lyric line that contains a section sign (§) followed by a letter no longer turns the text coloured, bold or flickering in the sky, the top bar or the song library; the sign and its letter are left out.
- **Very long lyric lines.** A very long line, such as plain lyrics that arrive as one line or a long Chinese or Japanese line, no longer freezes or slows the game in the Arc layout or makes it stutter in the World layout. In the Arc layout such a line now scrolls so the words being sung stay in front of you (before, they could be above the view and the sky looked empty).
- **Safer downloads.** An album cover address that points at a shared folder on another computer is no longer opened (on Windows that could have sent your login details to that computer). An album cover link from the internet can no longer redirect the game to this computer or your home network. Links your music player gives directly still work, so album covers from a music server on your own network keep showing. Replies from the lyrics sites are limited in size and time. A lyrics file with a long run of odd characters can no longer slow the lyrics down. Odd data from the NetEase backup no longer makes a song's lyrics search fail for good.
- **Update downloads.** An update download that stops halfway is now given up after 5 minutes, instead of holding the update for the rest of the session. The unfinished download is removed from your mods folder, and so is one left over from an earlier run.
- **Spotify accounts.** Signing in to another Spotify account now opens your own playlists without restarting the game.
- **Lyrics site errors.** An error for one odd song title no longer switches the lyrics site (LRCLIB) off for two minutes. Only a site that is really down or too busy does, and even then a song the backup site (NetEase) doesn't have is still asked from LRCLIB. When LRCLIB says it is too busy, the mod now waits as long as it asks before asking again, even if it names a time instead of a number of seconds.
- **Slide apart.** In the World layout, two words that overlap by a sliver side by side now part sideways instead of sliding into each other and jittering or stacking.
- **Spotify sign-in fixes.** Pasting a different Client ID while a sign-in waits in the browser now cancels that sign-in, instead of ending in a silent sign-out. A broken reply from Spotify (for example a network login page) no longer stops the sign-in or the polling with no message, and a failed sign-in never says "null".
- **Settings from a newer version.** When a newer SkyLyrics (or a newer Minecraft version of the mod sharing the folder) wrote the settings file, an older one no longer wipes the settings it doesn't know when you change a setting. Saved song timings for titles that carry hidden text-direction marks are found again.
- **Lazy follow.** Joining another world no longer keeps the old world's anchor, so the lyrics and sky effects start where you look. A word blown away by the Blow leave no longer vanishes early near the edge of the view.
- **Updates with a linked mod file.** If the mod's file is linked into the mods folder from somewhere else (Nix or GNU Stow, for example), you were never told about a new version. Now you are told, though it can't install itself there. On Linux and Mac, an update the mod installs keeps the old file's permissions.
- **Words left behind on fast moves.** In the World layout, the words now travel with you when you move very fast (a long fall, a hard knock) and, with **Elytra mode** on, when you launch with a Riptide trident, instead of being left behind and replaced by new ones. Teleporting still leaves them where they were.
- **Narrator in the tour and settings.** The intro tour now reads its page and the chosen look and layout, and the "<" and ">" buttons are called "Previous look" and "Next look"; the keyboard stays on the button you pressed. In the settings, Left, Right and Space no longer change the setting under the mouse before the mouse has moved: the keyboard first lands on the first setting and says it. Ctrl+Tab also says the setting it lands on, a search result that its tab is hiding says "not in use now", times are read as a number of seconds, and **Timing** says which way is late and early.
- **Song library and keyboard.** Enter and Esc are now spoken: the "Starting" and "Playing" messages, the name of a playlist when it opens or closes, "Loading", "Nothing found" and "No liked songs yet", how many results a search found, and that a song is a button or a playlist opens with Enter. The grid, shelf and carousel buttons, the recent searches and the **Open Music tab** button can now be reached with the keyboard (press Up from the top row of songs, then Left and Right; Down goes back).
- **Rain at night.** On 1.21.11 and newer, rain at night no longer makes the lyrics take daytime colours and a dark edge; clear weather looks as before at every time of day.
- **Old night sky when joining a world.** Joining a world right after leaving one at night no longer flashes the old night sky for half a second.
- **Lyrics when the lyrics site is busy (issue #1).** When LRCLIB's exact lookup is busy, the mod searches the site instead of saying it can't reach the lyrics sites.
- **Lyrics files.** Files that write times with a comma (`[00:10,50]`) load; lines at the very start no longer get squashed together when a file shifts its timing, and an original line and its translation stay together; NetEase's "pure music, please enjoy" note and a plain "Instrumental" count as instrumental; real plain lyrics are used when the timed copy has only time stamps.
- **A broken lyrics file can't freeze the game.** One enormous line or a huge number of lines is cut down, and very long song names are shortened (saved timings still match).
- **Menu background on 1.21.4 and 1.21.5.** The settings and the song library, opened from the title screen, show the menu background instead of black.
- **Hand-edited settings.** A number written as NaN or Infinity resets that setting to its default instead of its smallest value, and an empty settings file counts as a fresh start.

### Faster

- **Lighter lyrics and Galaxy.** Lines and Arc lyrics and the Galaxy sky do less work each frame.
- **Lighter Aurora and Nebula.** The default Aurora sky, the Nebula clouds and stars, and the constellations skip the parts behind you or off the side of the screen. They look the same and cost less each frame.
- **Lighter top bar and Record card.** The bar keeps its line laid out instead of measuring it again every frame, and the card keeps its times and cut titles. Nothing looks different.
- **Lighter sky effects.** The Moonlight clouds, the Comet streamers and the eclipse corona do less work each frame.
- **Lighter settings window.** The settings window lays out each row once per frame instead of several times, and remembers the right-to-left text it has already put in order. Nothing looks different.
- **Smaller saved album covers.** Album covers are saved as small 128-pixel pictures, so they load faster and take less disk space, and they are made in memory instead of through a temporary file.
- **No hitch when a setting changes.** Settings are saved in the background, so pressing a timing key or closing the settings no longer makes the game pause for a moment while the file is written (most noticeable on Windows when an antivirus or OneDrive holds the file). A change made right before you quit is still saved.

### Changed

- **At most three flashes a second.** When lines come very quickly, the glow, crosshair, hat and sky flashes no longer restart for every line: they start at most three times a second. Normal songs look the same.
- **No lyrics rather than the wrong lyrics.** When the lyrics site (LRCLIB) doesn't have the song, the mod no longer shows lyrics from a different song, even one by the same artist, so such a song now shows none. A title with a translation or romanisation in brackets still finds its lyrics.
- **Pauses in the lyrics.** A line that is only "(Instrumental)", "(music)", "Instrumental", "♪ instrumental ♪", "(Intro)", "(Outro)", "(Solo)" or a note emoji now counts as a pause instead of being shown as words. A line that is just "Music" is still sung. A line starting with a part tag such as "[Chorus] words" no longer shows the tag.
- **Welcome tour and texts.** The tour says which apps SkyLyrics can read on a Mac (Music and Spotify, not browsers), that macOS will ask for permission, and that signing in to Spotify is optional and needs Premium and a free developer app. On a Mac, the permission texts say "your launcher". The Music tab says "No Spotify or Music playing". The Hebrew texts speak in the plural, write Spotify and Minecraft in Hebrew letters, and say "no access" for the internet error.
- **Reset all.** **Reset all** keeps your intro tour done, your update choice, your Spotify Client ID, your per-song timings and your recent searches.
- **Synced lyrics first.** When the lyrics site's best match for a song has only plain lyrics, the mod also looks for a synced copy before settling for the plain one. A lyrics file with only tags and no lines no longer counts as an answer.
- **One name for the album cover.** The album picture is called "album cover" everywhere in the settings and help pages.
- **Lyrics must fit the song.** A copy of the lyrics whose song length is more than 20 seconds off your song's is no longer used (it was often another version's lyrics).
- **Saved lyrics checked once more.** Lyrics saved by version 0.8.0 or older are checked again the next time you play the song. If the lyrics site has other lyrics for it, they replace the saved ones. If it has none, the saved ones stay for that play and are looked up fresh the next time.
- **Themes keep your other settings.** Picking a theme now changes only what themes set (the layout, colours, fonts, glow, size, opacity, animation, sky and a few more). Settings no theme touches, such as **Karaoke fill**, **Shadow** and **Two-tone**, stay as you set them, and the theme still shows as picked (not Custom).
- **Last line fades.** In Lines and Arc, a line that ended more than a second and a half ago (the last lyric during the outro, or a line before a long instrumental part) fades out.
- **Floating distance.** With Floating placement, every step of the **Distance** slider now moves the lyrics nearer or farther (before, 8 to 24 were all the same distance, and so were 96 to 160). They keep the same size on screen, so you see it as you walk past them or with **See through blocks** off. The default is unchanged.
- **Spotify asks less.** With Spotify signed in, when the lyrics are off and none of the mod's screens is open, the mod asks Spotify for the song only every 15 seconds. When Spotify keeps failing, the mod waits longer each time before asking again, but no longer than 30 seconds (a Spotify app that doesn't know your account waits a minute). When Spotify says it is busy, the mod waits as long as Spotify asks (up to 5 minutes).
- **Timing sliders.** The **Timing** and **This song** sliders now reach 5 seconds either way.
- **Clearer Spotify setup.** With no Client ID pasted, the Music tab now says "Paste your Client ID first" and no "can't read your music player" pop-up appears. The old "Spotify sign-in needs port" line goes away when you press **Sign in** or **Sign out**. A bad connection while signing in or loading the song library says "Can't reach the internet or Spotify" instead of a raw error. The sign-in page opened in your browser reads right to left for Hebrew.
- **Clearer lyrics messages.** A lyrics site that answers with an odd error shows "no lyrics" instead of blaming your internet. On a Mac, the "Nothing playing" bar in the settings no longer suggests browsers, and it stays quiet while the music player can't be read.
- **Clearer setting texts.** The **Hide lyrics** card is now **Hide**, because its rows also hide the top bar, the **Record card** and the sky effects. The texts of **Karaoke fill** (it lights up the top bar's words too), **Top bar**, **Accent colour**, **Draw on top**, **Song name only on change**, **Hide in multiplayer**, **Show underground too** and **This song** now say what the setting really does. **Show underground too** only shows when **See through blocks** is off, since otherwise it changes nothing. **Karaoke fill** also shows in World while the top bar shows lyrics. **Depth** only shows in Arc, the one layout that draws it, and **Shadow** is hidden in Arc while **Depth** is on, since Depth replaces it there. The settings window's footer says just "Esc to close" when **Open settings** has no key, and the **Show or hide lyrics** key now says "Lyrics on" or "Lyrics off" above the hotbar. In a small window, the choices in a row of buttons (like the **Record card**'s corner) keep a gap between names instead of touching.
- **Help pages.** The Troubleshooting page and FAQ now say what to expect with Replay Mod and Flashback recordings (the lyrics follow the music playing when you render, not when you recorded) and with Distant Horizons (which night skies can show in front of far-away terrain).
- **Game log.** The mod's lines in the game log no longer show song names or your home folder name, and a problem that repeats (offline, a failed save) is written once, so the log is safe to attach to a bug report.
- **Hebrew.** A few smoother lines (Draw on top, Karaoke fill, the Mac browser note).
